item.title: Netgear patches three router vulnerabilities, urges updates
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Netgear patches three flaws in its routers and extenders. Update now
Netgear has patched three security flaws in its routers and extenders. The vulnerabilities, classified as moderately severe, allow attackers to execute remote commands or bypass admin login credentials. Affected models include CAX30, RAX30, RAX5, RAXE300, EX3700, RAX28, RAX29, and RAX30. CVE-2026-11732 enables unauthorized command execution if an attacker has local network access, while CVE-2026-11731 allows bypassing admin login on specific models. The EX3700 and EX6120 extenders are vulnerable to session hijacking via CVE-2026-11730. Netgear recommends immediate firmware updates for supported devices and replacement of unsupported models like R7000, RAX40, and R7300DST, which no longer receive security patches. Additional vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-9218 and others, affect older models. Users are advised to enable automatic updates where available.

item.title: Mistral Releases Trillion-Parameter AI Model for Cybersecurity
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
French AI firm Mistral released the weights for its trillion-parameter open-source model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), dubbed 'Le Chonk,' enabling businesses and governments to deploy the system independently. The move positions Mistral against closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic, emphasizing control over data and systems in cybersecurity. CEO Arthur Mensch argued AI should 'be a tool for empowerment, not dominance,' highlighting ML4's 'state-of-the-art performance' at lower compute costs. Mistral claims ML4 outperforms GLM-5.3, a leading open model, by using 47% fewer tokens per task. The model also ranks highest among open models in agentic coding tasks. Available on Hugging Face and via API, ML4 targets cybersecurity with capabilities to detect and respond to threats. Pierre Stock, Mistral's VP of Science, stressed open-source access allows organizations to 'own frontier AI' and deploy it on-premises. He warned of malicious actors exploiting AI but cautioned against overreacting, calling the security challenge 'solvable.'

item.title: Google Introduces 'Immersive Explorations' for Educational Learning
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: 'Immersive Explorations' in Gemini is a visual adventure for traversing stellar topics
Google introduced 'Immersive Explorations' in its Gemini student hub, offering a visual learning tool that allows users to explore topics through layered visuals. The feature enables students to interact with content by clicking through images to uncover details about subjects like Quasars, dinosaurs, molecular structures, and lightning physics. Available in English, Indonesian, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, French, and simplified Chinese, the tool aims to replace traditional text-based learning with interactive exploration. Google emphasized that users can view the broader context of a topic while diving into specific elements. The update builds on previous Gemini enhancements for education, including AI-driven lesson planning tools in the Classrooms app and a 'Coach' feature for guided learning. The new tool is accessible now within the Gemini app, expanding Google's efforts to integrate AI into educational platforms for students and teachers.

item.title: Google Gemini Lets Users Edit Files Directly in Chat
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Digital Trends Original headline: Google Gemini Now Allows Direct File Editing Within Chat Conversations
Google has updated its Gemini AI model to let users generate, preview, and edit files like PDFs, Google Docs, Sheets, Markdown, TXT, and code directly within chat conversations. PDF editing is available on web and mobile, while other formats are limited to web access. Users can expand documents to full-screen mode, highlight text for revisions, or request insights like converting tables to graphs. The feature builds on prior file-generation capabilities, streamlining tasks such as creating study guides or refining reports. Digital Trends highlighted its value for students and professionals handling documents, enabling real-time edits without restarting workflows. The update is available in regions where Gemini is supported and in multiple languages. Google also recently released Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon, which performed well in AI benchmarks. File-editing tools are now accessible to all users in supported areas, enhancing Gemini's productivity features.

item.title: Fake PS5 Emulators Steal Gamers' Passwords
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Fake PS5 emulators are being used to steal gamers' passwords
Malicious GitHub repositories impersonating legitimate PS5 emulation tools AnyPS5 and Kyttyps5 are distributing malware that steals gamers' passwords. The malware uses self-signed certificates with fake company names and creation dates, suggesting automated deployment. Upon infection, a cleanup script deletes all traces of the malware within two minutes. The payload, an infostealer protected by a commercial packer, targets real machines by bypassing security checks for virtual environments or cloud servers. It evades detection by modifying Microsoft Defender settings. Users are advised to verify repository ownership, check download links, and avoid third-party sources. If compromised, disconnect from the internet and run antivirus scans. The attack exploits the popularity of PS5 emulation, which is expected to grow with GTA 6's 2026 console release. The malware's rapid repository rotation suggests GitHub may not be the sole distribution channel.

item.title: AI Creates Photoshop Clone in One Day, Experts Weigh In
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: AI Built a Photoshop Clone in a Day. I Asked Experts What Happens Next
AI tools can generate functional software, including a Photoshop clone called PhotoCraft, in under a day. Brandon Thomas, founder of ArtCraft, developed PhotoCraft using AI prompts, spending 24 hours to create the first version. He avoided accessing Photoshop's source code, relying instead on screenshots and architectural planning. Photopea, a free Photoshop alternative, took 14 years to develop without AI. Experts debate AI's impact: Thomas claims AI can replicate any software, while Photopea creator Ivan Kutskir doubts AI apps will replace established tools soon. ArtCraft's apps, like LightCraft, closely mimic Adobe products but lack some advanced features. LibreOffice's Italo Vignoli emphasizes community support as crucial for non-technical users, noting ArtCraft has a growing Discord community. However, AI apps face reliability and security concerns, with developers criticizing them as buggy and insecure. Despite these issues, AI's ability to rapidly create complex software raises legal and ethical questions about intellectual property and competition.

item.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive acquires ADT for $15.3 billion
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
Thrive Holdings, a holding company backed by OpenAI and Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital, acquired ADT for $10 per share, valuing the deal at $7.6 billion in equity and $15.3 billion in total enterprise value. The acquisition aims to expand Thrive's smart home security business, with ADT forming its foundation. OpenAI will provide AI models, technology, and engineers to Thrive's portfolio. Neither company disclosed specific AI-powered products but plan to invest in new offerings. ADT already partners with Apple and Google, and the deal aligns with growing AI-driven physical security trends. The move follows Apple's entry into smart home security and Amazon's updates to its smart home line. Thrive Holdings, which owns over 75 companies, seeks to revitalize them with AI. The deal underscores the expanding role of AI in physical security, with potential future innovations like AI dog robots as security guards.

item.title: Intel's 6W Moon Lake Chips Aim to Power Efficient, Quiet Laptops
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Intel’s 6W Moon Lake chips could make budget laptops cooler, quieter, and more efficient at a cost
Intel is developing Moon Lake chips, a new family of entry-level laptop processors with a 6W thermal design power (TDP) rating. This is significantly lower than the 10W TDP of current Core Series 3 chips. The design uses four low-power LPE cores instead of performance cores, targeting lighter workloads. Laptop makers could potentially remove cooling fans and extend battery life due to reduced power consumption. The 18A manufacturing process and 8-16GB memory could enable affordable, quiet laptops for basic tasks like browsing and document work. However, Moon Lake lacks performance cores, limiting capabilities for heavy editing or gaming. Manufacturers might increase TDP to 15W for extra performance, but at the cost of more heat and fan noise. Moon Lake would sit below the Core Series 3 lineup, with no official release date confirmed. Intel has not verified details, so the information remains speculative.

item.title: AO3 Outage Extended Due to Security Incident
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Engadget Original headline: Fan Fiction Site AO3 Faces Extended Outage Amid Security Incident
Archive of Our Own (AO3) faces an extended outage lasting up to four weeks due to a security incident. The Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), which operates the site, initially planned brief maintenance but extended the downtime after discovering the issue. The outage began October 23 and has raised concerns about data security. OTW confirmed the site’s database remains intact, though it has not disclosed specifics about the incident. Users are advised to change passwords on other platforms if they reused AO3 credentials. Speculation linked the outage to recent PHP vulnerabilities, but AO3 uses Ruby on Rails, making such a connection unlikely. OTW noted its volunteer engineering team may contribute to slower resolution times. The organization also mentioned issues with email notifications and search functionality during the outage. Fanlore, OTW’s sister platform, previously faced a PHP-related outage. OTW has not confirmed whether the current incident involves PHP vulnerabilities or provided further details on recovery steps. Users are urged to monitor official updates for further information.

item.title: US Air Force uses AI to improve aerial refuelling error detection
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: The US Air Force wants to use AI to help with its mid-air refuelling problems
The US Air Force is developing AI technology to detect errors during aerial refuelling operations. The system will analyze footage from tanker aircraft cameras to monitor aircraft speed, alignment, positioning, and approach velocity. It aims to provide detailed, consistent performance evaluations by identifying deviations from expected flight conditions and generating feedback for instructors. Current assessments rely heavily on human observation and manual reviews, which can lead to inconsistent judgments. The AI will use computer vision and machine learning to track interactions between tankers and receivers, including refuelling boom movements. Graphical overlays and color-coded performance maps will highlight critical events. The project, under the Small Business Innovation Research programme, seeks solutions for the KC-46 Pegasus tanker, which uses remote vision systems for fuel transfer. Developers must submit proposals by November 25 2026. The technology could later integrate with flight simulators, VR, and AR training tools. Potential applications extend beyond refuelling to other aviation activities within the Department of Defense.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Android Status Bar Icons: 12 Key Symbols Explained
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: From keys to dots: 12 mystery Android status bar icons you should know
Google's Android setup process explains basic phone functions but leaves status bar icons unexplained. Key icons include network signals (H, LTE, 5G) indicating connectivity strength and type. Wi-Fi icons show connection status, with exclamation marks signaling issues. Bluetooth and NFC icons confirm device pairing, though Pixels lack NFC visibility. Battery indicators change color based on charge levels, and a plus sign appears with battery saver. New colorful dots in the status bar signal app activity: green for camera/microphone use, blue for location access. VPNs appear as key icons, and airplane mode uses a distinct symbol. Some icons vary by manufacturer, like Pixel's absence of NFC. Users are advised to recognize these symbols for troubleshooting and privacy awareness, and to investigate unfamiliar icons via screenshots if needed.

item.title: SK Hynix Predicts Memory Shortage to Last Until 2030
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: SK Hynix now expects the memory shortage to last until 2030
SK Hynix expects the global memory shortage to persist until 2030, according to its quarterly report. The company attributes this to surging demand from AI data centers, robotics, and other industries adopting AI technologies. Building new semiconductor factories takes years, delaying supply growth. Manufacturers prioritize enterprise-grade memory chips for AI servers, limiting consumer RAM availability and driving up prices. SK Hynix has secured long-term supply agreements for 2027-2028 and plans a $13 billion fabrication plant operational by 2030. Samsung also projects shortages until 2028. Consumer devices reliant on RAM and storage will face continued supply constraints and higher costs.

item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon with Enhanced Cybersecurity Features
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: With Gemini 4 Carbon, Google Touts Big Leap in Cybersecurity Capabilities
Google released the Gemini 4 Carbon model, claiming it represents a major advancement in cybersecurity capabilities. The model outperforms previous versions like Gemini 4 Argon, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 across coding, knowledge work, science, math, and cybersecurity benchmarks. Carbon can detect critical vulnerabilities, validate them, and generate high-quality patches. It also resists prompt injections, with internal tests showing a 0.0% attack success rate compared to Argon’s 0.7% and Claude Opus 5.5’s 1.0%. Carbon will initially be available to a subset of cyber defenders at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with broader access planned through Google’s Fairwind Program. Developers, businesses, and consumers will gain access as soon as possible.

item.title: Binance Announces $6.3 Billion Crypto Hack, Largest Ever
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo, TechCrunch, PCMag Original headline: Binance Confirms $6.3 Billion Crypto Hack, Largest in History
Binance confirmed a major security breach resulting in $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency losses, the largest crypto hack in history. The incident involved a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, allowing an attacker to access a service container and execute unauthorized withdrawals. At least $2.54 billion in stablecoins was frozen, with additional funds potentially affected. Major stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $1.56 billion and $823 million respectively. Cryptocurrency prices dropped sharply, with Bitcoin falling 2.8%, Ethereum 3.6%, and BNB 6.9%. The breach exceeds the previous record of $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in 2025. Binance co-CEO Yi He temporarily disabled withdrawals, citing unresolved security concerns. Founder Changpeng Zhao stated user funds are safe, with emergency SAFU funds covering losses. Analysts estimate stolen amounts between $1.7 billion and over $5.7 billion, with some tools suggesting more than $5.8 billion may have left the network. Security researchers highlighted vulnerabilities in crypto infrastructure, including third-party software and internet-connected wallets.

item.title: Polymarket Freezes Trading After Hackers Steal Millions via Third-Party Service
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Polymarket Temporarily Froze Trading After Hackers Reportedly Stole Millions Via Third-Party Service
Hackers breached Polymarket's international exchange, stealing an undisclosed amount of user funds through a compromised third-party service, DebugBear. The incident, reported by CNBC, originated from DebugBear's Real User Monitoring (RUM) service, which was hacked and used to siphon funds. Polymarket suspended trading and switched to 'cancel-only mode' after DebugBear alerted users to an 'ongoing security incident.' The breach reportedly led to unauthorized withdrawals, with analytics showing approximately $2.65 million in tokens stolen. Polymarket US, a federally regulated exchange, was unaffected. The company stated it had reported the incident to police and would reimburse impacted customers. DebugBear's website was inaccessible, and attempts to contact them failed. Polymarket has faced prior security issues, including a $3.1 million phishing attack and a $520,000 theft. The company recently raised $1 billion in funding, with Donald Trump Jr. as a partner. Regulatory scrutiny over prediction markets intensified, with Democrats potentially pushing for stricter oversight amid midterm elections. Polymarket and Kalshi have faced accusations of enabling insider trading and regulatory evasion.

item.title: SuperMe raises $20M for AI expert network
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: SuperMe raises $20M for its network of AI expert profiles
SuperMe raised $20 million in funding led by Forerunner’s Kirsten Green, with Greylock Partners participating. Founded in 2024 by Casey Winters and Ludo Antonov, the startup builds an AI network connecting users with expert knowledge. Users submit questions via chatbots, which then assemble groups of AI profiles based on expertise. The platform aggregates data from public sources and connected apps to create expert profiles, ensuring sensitive info isn’t shared in answers. SuperMe is free but plans to limit free question counts and offer paid access. It also integrates with MCP to let AI chatbots access external tools. The startup, with 13 employees, is hiring to enhance AI models and expand expert networks. Green called SuperMe well-positioned to create a collaborative AI-human platform, emphasizing the need for shared knowledge as the field evolves.

item.title: Fujifilm to Boost Magnetic Tape Production 5x Amid AI Storage Demand
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Fujifilm plans 5x production boost of 100TB magnetic storage tapes driven by skyrocketing AI storage demand
Fujifilm plans to increase magnetic tape production by five times, investing 10 billion yen to expand its Odawara plant. The move aims to meet rising demand for 100TB tapes used in AI data centers, marking the company's largest tape storage investment in over 20 years. Magnetic tapes remain popular for long-term data backup due to their durability, low cost, and environmental benefits compared to SSDs and HDDs. While LTO technology allows for up to 365TB per cartridge, SSDs max out at 256TB. Fujifilm is not alone in capitalizing on AI-driven storage needs; Toshiba, Seagate, WD, Kioxia, and SanDisk are also expanding capacities. The AI data center boom has triggered a global shortage, driving up prices and shifting manufacturer focus toward enterprise markets.

item.title: Google Fixes Bug Hiding Edited Photos from Other Apps
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Google fixes an annoying Photos bug that hid edited images from other apps
Google has resolved a bug that prevented edited images from appearing in other apps like messaging and social media. Users previously faced issues where edited photos in Google Photos were hidden from the image picker, forcing some to save copies instead of overwriting originals. The fix was confirmed by APK Mirror founder Artem Russakovskii and 9to5Google. This follows another recent issue where the Share, Edit, Add to, and Trash buttons became unresponsive on certain devices after edits, which Google addressed swiftly. The updates aim to improve app integration and user experience for Android users.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Windows 11's Point-in-Time Restore Lets Users Revert System State
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Oops! Use this new Windows 11 setting to roll back recent system damage
Windows 11's Point-in-Time Restore (PITR) feature allows users to revert the system to a previous state. Available in version 24H2 and on drives of at least 200GB, PITR restores the operating system, apps, settings, and personal files to a selected restore point. It automatically creates restore points every 24 hours, retaining them for up to 72 hours. Users can manually enable the feature in Settings or via the recovery environment. Restore points prior to system issues can be selected, but changes made after the restore point will be lost. Cloud-synced files and other drives remain unaffected. The process requires uninterrupted operation and may prompt for BitLocker recovery keys. PITR is not a substitute for regular backups, which are still recommended for long-term data protection. Managed devices in corporate environments may have different settings applied by administrators.

item.title: Waymo partners with Toyota to supply robotaxis in Japan and U.K.
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the U.K.
Waymo will test autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan starting next year as part of a partnership to supply electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in Japan and the U.K. Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X models at its Takaoka factory and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system. Initial testing will focus on Japan, with plans to deploy the vehicles in right-hand driving countries like the U.K., where Waymo has been testing Jaguar I-Pace vehicles. The partnership, announced after an 18-month preliminary agreement, currently resembles a conventional supplier deal but may expand to include Waymo’s autonomous technology in personally owned Toyota vehicles. Both companies also plan to explore future initiatives using Waymo’s real-world data to enhance road safety. Hiroki Nakajima, Toyota’s executive vice president, stated the collaboration aims to scale the technology through Waymo’s ride-hailing service and improve road safety by integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure.

item.title: Ubisoft Confirms No New Assassin's Creed Remakes, Focuses on New Projects
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: Ubisoft Announces Assassin's Creed Updates, Including No New Remakes
Ubisoft confirmed no new Assassin's Creed remakes are in development, focusing instead on original projects. The Black Flag Resynced remake will receive New Game+ and Nightmare Mode, with Valhalla getting New Game+ on November 5. Digital Trends noted Valhalla's update includes a power system for Eivor, new gear upgrades with Mithril, and additional content. Black Flag Resynced also adds extra finishers, trinkets, and customization. Ubisoft mentioned progress on multiplayer project Invictus and the 2027 release of Hexe's first major update. Netflix's live-action series nears completion with Hannah Peel composing the soundtrack. The franchise will celebrate its 20th anniversary in 2027 with events and reveals. Current-gen console updates for Valhalla will be shared soon.

item.title: Google revamps Android 17 with app lock and bug fixes in QPR3 Beta 3
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google brings back app lock in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3
Google released Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 with 26 bug fixes and usability improvements. The update brings back app lock, allowing users to restrict access to sensitive apps. App bubbles are now accessible via the Recents menu, and a camera shortcut is added to Quick Settings. Lock screen AM/PM display and previously removed blur effects are restored. Fixes address screen flickering, foldable display issues, webcam quality, and Bluetooth/Wi-Fi connectivity problems. The update targets Pixel 6a and newer devices with build numbers DP11.261016.003 and DP11.261016.004. Google warns users to back up data before installing beta software. Android 17 QPR2 is expected to stabilize by late 2026, with QPR3 aiming for 2027 release.

item.title: GPU Power Limit Slider Can Dramatically Reduce Performance
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: This tiny slider is tanking your GPU performance
A GPU's power limit slider can drastically reduce performance. Modern GPUs adjust clock speeds and voltages based on power availability, but restricting the power budget through this slider can throttle performance. Lowering the power limit below 100% restricts how much power the GPU can draw, potentially preventing it from sustaining boost clocks. Tools like MSI Afterburner and AMD Adrenalin allow users to adjust this setting, with 100% representing the default power budget. Some users may have inadvertently lowered the slider through undervolting, noise reduction presets, or outdated tuning profiles. Testing shows significant performance differences: reducing the RTX 4090's power limit to 50% cut gaming performance by 23%, while 80% caused only a 2.3% drop. Performance loss varies by GPU model and workload, with GPU-heavy games suffering more. Resetting the slider to 100% can restore lost frames, though efficiency gains may come at the cost of performance. Users should check their GPU tuning software to identify and adjust the power limit setting.

item.title: Company Develops Solar System with Integrated Backup
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Turning a solar power system into its own backup
Concentrated solar power uses mirrors to generate heat for electricity, once seen as viable for 24/7 power. However, plummeting photovoltaic costs made solar panels the cheapest option, pushing concentrated solar to compete with batteries and gas plants. A startup now claims its system integrates fossil-fuel backup with solar thermal hardware, reducing the need for separate facilities. The technology relies on heliostats to focus sunlight on a tower, heating fluid to drive turbines or store energy. Despite variations like trough mirrors and different fluids, challenges like moving parts and corrosion have kept costs higher than PV. The company’s approach aims to merge solar thermal with backup systems, potentially lowering expenses while addressing intermittency issues.

item.title: Microsoft Updates Windows 11 with Customizable Right-Click Menu and Cloud Rebuild Feature
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Digital Trends, PCWorld Original headline: Microsoft Rolls Out Windows 11 Update to Customize Right-Click Menu and Introduce Cloud Rebuild Feature
Microsoft is rolling out a major Windows 11 update, KB5127936, for versions 25H2 and 26H2. The update allows users to customize the right-click menu by rearranging, hiding, or enabling commands like 'Send To' and 'Create Shortcut.' It replaces specialized icons with text options for actions like 'Cut,' 'Copy,' and 'Paste,' aiming to restore a Windows 10-style layout. Users can also manage third-party app extensions, choosing whether they appear in the main menu or submenus. The redesign improves performance with faster load times and reduced clutter. The rollout is gradual, with instructions available via Windows Update settings. The update coincides with Microsoft’s quarterly financial report, which noted declining PC revenue, highlighting the company’s focus on enhancing user experience. A new recovery feature, Cloud Rebuild, lets users reinstall Windows 11 from the cloud without external media, though it functions as a fresh installation, erasing existing apps and files. Users are advised to sanitize system drives before using it. The changes reflect Microsoft’s effort to balance innovation with user preferences, as noted by Digital Trends. Minor adjustments to Xbox mode and settings are also included, though details were not specified.

item.title: Google Expands AI Mode Ads to Additional Countries
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Google brings AI Mode advertisements to more countries
Google is expanding AI Mode advertisements to additional countries. The feature will show sponsored content in Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Singapore. Brazil, Mexico, and the UK will receive ads later this year, with the US also getting 'multiturn' ads that appear in follow-up queries. The move follows Alphabet's Q3 earnings call, where executives noted AI Mode had lower monetization than costs but showed 'promising results.' After launching AI Mode in the US in May 2025, Google began testing ads there in November, aiming to improve profitability.

item.title: Meta Alerts Parents on Teens' Repeated Self-Harm Searches on Facebook
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Meta will now alert parents if teens 'repeatedly' search for self-harm content on Facebook
Meta is expanding parental notifications for teens' searches related to self-harm and suicide risk. Parents will receive alerts if their teen 'repeatedly' searches for self-harm content on Facebook within a short period. The company also notifies parents if a teen's conversation with Meta AI suggests potential suicide or self-harm risk. Meta remains vague about exact criteria, stating alerts are triggered by multiple searches in a short timeframe while avoiding unnecessary notifications. Parents receive alerts via text, email, WhatsApp, or app notifications but are not provided specific search terms or chat details. The feature is part of Meta's teen account initiative, which allows parents to supervise privacy settings and limit exposure to sensitive content. The update aims to give caregivers more control over teens' online activity. Crisis resources are listed for those in need.

item.title: FromSoftware delays The Duskbloods until 2027
item.description:
Source: Engadget
FromSoftware has delayed The Duskbloods to 2027, citing the need to refine game rules and balance. The multiplayer game, announced in April 2025 during a Switch 2 showcase, was initially set for this year but now faces a later release. The studio cited feedback from an August network test, which showed interest in core concepts like combat and strategic depth, prompting the delay to allow further adjustments. This follows a pattern of delays for Switch 2, including a postponed Elden Ring port that faced performance issues. The delay may also account for competition from upcoming titles like Grand Theft Auto 6 and the Ocarina of Time remake, which are expected to dominate player attention this year.

item.title: Intel Selling All Affordable Laptop Chips Amid High Demand
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Intel says it’s selling every affordable laptop chip it can make
Intel’s CEO Lip-Bu Tan and CFO David Zinsner reported that demand for budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips is outpacing supply, with the chips now sold out. Zinsner highlighted significant growth in Wildcat Lake sales, noting their cost-optimized design aligns with market focus. The chips are used in affordable Windows laptops like the Dell XPS 13 and HP Omnibook 5 14, often with 8GB RAM. Intel’s Zinsner warned of ongoing memory shortages, stating the company is “not optimistic about next year in terms of memory” and expects supply issues to persist into 2027. He noted SK Hynix predicts the RAM shortage could last until 2030. Tan acknowledged a PC demand slowdown linked to AI-driven supply chain challenges, while Zinsner asserted the PC industry will still experience a renaissance despite these hurdles.

item.title: Ultrahuman's Ring Pro Launches in U.S. with In-Store Fitting at Best Buy
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Ultrahuman's Ring Pro arrives in the US—consumers can get it fitted in-store, but only at Best Buy
Ultrahuman's Ring Pro is now available in the U.S. without pre-order delays. The smart ring can be purchased online at Ultrahuman, Target, Walmart, and Best Buy, with 300 Best Buy locations offering in-store fitting and same-day pickup. Priced at $479, the device features a 15-day battery life (45 days with the included charging case), enhanced memory for up to 250 days of health data, a titanium build, and a 'Find My Case' feature. CEO Mohit Kumar praised the U.S. launch, allowing customers to avoid delays. The Ring Pro also includes haptic feedback, LED battery indicators, and no subscription required for health tracking. It is available in sizes 5 through 14. Ultrahuman plans to expand in-store availability to Target and Walmart over the next few weeks.

item.title: Starlink Implements Dynamic Pricing with Location-Based Rate Changes
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Starlink Tests Dynamic Pricing. Bills Could Be 20% Higher Depending on Location
SpaceX’s Starlink is introducing quarterly dynamic pricing for Residential internet plans in select areas, with potential increases or decreases based on supply and demand. Users in Kansas and Missouri received emails notifying them of changes, citing growing satellite capacity and subscriber numbers as factors. A Missouri user’s 100 Mbps plan rose from $50 to $60.50, while another’s Max plan increased to $156 from $130. In Kansas City, prices are lower: $49.50, $76.50, and $117 for 100 Mbps, 200 Mbps, and Max plans, respectively. Marysville, Kansas, offers even lower rates. Starlink.com reflects max 20% increases or decreases. Tim Belfall reports similar decreases in the UK. A Reddit user noted some customers face higher bills while others see reductions, describing it as a system where price cuts for some are funded by others’ higher costs. SpaceX did not comment on the policy, which could lead to more frequent price adjustments.

item.title: DoorDash Acquires Instacart in $17B Deal, Merging Subscriptions
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Doordash is acquiring Instacart. For you, that means one less subscription, eventually.
DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart in a $17 billion cash-and-stock deal, expected to close by late 2027 or early 2028. The merger combines DoorDash’s delivery network with Instacart’s grocery technology, offering customers access to 50,000 additional stores and potential faster deliveries. DashPass and Instacart+ subscriptions will merge into a single service, though the new pricing remains undisclosed. Originally, DashPass cost $9.99/month with $20 monthly savings, while Instacart+ offered free delivery over $35 orders and 5% credit back for $9.99/month. Local businesses can partner with both platforms, and delivery drivers will handle combined orders. The companies will operate separately until regulatory approval. Discussions about the merger began in 2021, with Instacart going public in 2023 and both firms becoming profitable in 2024. Instacart recently launched initiatives like paying shoppers to film in stores.

item.title: Hacker Group Claims UNM Hospital Cyberattack, Apologizes, Offers $2500 Payments
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Hacker Group Claims UNM Hospital Cyberattack, Then Apologizes and Offers Patients $2,500
University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center faced a cybersecurity incident on Monday, prompting temporary ambulance diversions and suspended outpatient surgeries. Critical systems were restored by late afternoon, with officials stating core infrastructure remained unaffected. The university has not confirmed the attack was ransomware. A hacker group called BYOD claimed responsibility, listing the university on its data-leak site and alleging 36,000 devices were compromised, including student records and Oracle databases. BYOD later apologized, offering free decryption keys for hospital devices and $2,500 payments to affected patients. The group described its actions as 'pentesting' to expose security flaws. UNM stated it did not negotiate with the attackers and warned of scams exploiting public concern. The incident remains under criminal investigation, with no confirmation of BYOD’s claims. BYOD, a new ransomware group, previously targeted companies like Trump Mobile, leaking real customer data. A similar incident in 2023 saw LockBit apologize after an affiliate attacked a hospital, offering a free decryptor.

item.title: Virgin Galactic charges $750,000 for three minutes of weightlessness
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Virgin Galactic is charging $750,000 for three minutes of weightlessness, and nearly 700 people are already in the queue
Virgin Galactic is charging $750,000 for a three-minute weightlessness experience aboard its new Delta-class spaceplane Apeiron. The vehicle, which replaces the retired VSS Unity, can carry six passengers and is designed for up to eight flights monthly. Apeiron will reach 54.2 miles above Earth, below the Kármán line, after being launched by the Eve carrier plane. Commercial flights are expected to begin in early Q2 2027, with over 600 people already booked and more than 700 on the waiting list. The company projects $525 million in ticket sales from initial bookings. A second Delta-class spaceplane is set for late Q2 or early Q3 2027. With Blue Origin pausing suborbital flights, Virgin Galactic may dominate the market. The company faces the challenge of turning high-cost tickets into a sustainable business model.

item.title: ThermoWorks launches shorter RFX Meat Mini probe for small cuts
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: ThermoWorks debuts shorter version of its RFX Meat wireless probe for small cuts
ThermoWorks introduces the RFX Meat Mini, a shorter wireless temperature probe for small cuts. The 2.6-inch probe offers nearly identical performance to the full-sized RFX Meat, including four internal sensors, IP69K waterproofing, and 1,000°F temperature resistance. It replaces the 4.7-inch model, which was too long for smaller meats like salmon or filet mignon. The Mini’s maximum immersion line is 2.6 inches, with a minimum of 2.36 inches. Battery life is 48 hours versus 65 hours for the original. The Mini uses 433MHz radio frequency instead of Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, reducing interference from grill walls. It requires a RFX Gateway for connectivity, which is also needed for the original probe. The Mini is priced at $99, same as the full-sized model, with a 20% discount available when purchasing a Gateway or Starter Kit. ThermoWorks emphasizes the Mini’s suitability for home use, though commercial cooks may need the longer version for extended sessions.

item.title: Getac Launches Rugged Notebooks with AI Boost for Defense Markets
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Getac says its new rugged notebooks offer faster AI-powered processing than ever — and seem to be targeting military and defense customers
Getac has launched the B360X and B360X Pro rugged notebooks, targeting military and defense markets. The B360X, equipped with Intel's Core Ultra X7 358H chip, offers up to 180 TOPS of AI compute, while the B360X Pro, with a Core Ultra 7 356H, provides 98 TOPS. Both models feature 14-inch 1,400-nit displays, Wi-Fi 7, and MIL-STD ruggedness. The Pro is marketed for defense, with optional Nvidia RTX PRO 500 Blackwell GPU offering 294 AI TOPS. Intel's platform TOPS metric combines CPU, GPU, and NPU, with the X7's 12-core Arc graphics contributing 122 TOPS. The Pro's AI performance remains largely unchanged from last year's models. Getac highlights the B360X's exclusive X7 chip and the Pro's optional RTX upgrade for specialized AI tasks. Microsoft's Copilot+ branding is applied to both, though practical AI benefits remain debated. The B360X Pro's RTX card, while powerful, faces limitations due to 6GB VRAM and lacks published benchmarks.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Cyber Trust Mark for Smart Home Devices Set for 2027
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Biden-Era 'Cyber Trust Mark' May Finally Appear on Smart Home Gadgets in 2027
The US Cyber Trust Mark, a government-certified security label for smart home devices, is expected to debut on gadgets by 2027. The Federal Communications Commission finalized its design, with Commissioner Olivia Trusty overseeing the program. The label requires manufacturers to disclose data collection practices, security update schedules, and automatic update availability, similar to broadband provider disclosures. Consumers can scan QR codes for detailed product testing info, with certifications renewed every three years. The FCC may conduct ad-hoc device checks if needed. The initiative faces delays due to leadership changes, including UL Solutions' exit after an investigation into its ties to China. Connected-home security has lacked a standardized baseline, with many devices vulnerable to attacks due to weak defaults. While Germany and Singapore have similar programs, the US effort is still in development, with the Matter standard offering partial certification but limited vendor support.

item.title: Humanist Secures Religious Exemption From AI Work Use
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo, TechCrunch Original headline: Humanist Secures Religious Exemption From AI Use at Work
David Durman, a 45-year-old research administrator at the University of Kentucky, has secured a religious exemption from using artificial intelligence tools at work under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act. As a secular humanist, Durman argues AI undermines his belief in human flourishing and moral development. He told Religion News Service that critical thinking and human interaction are essential to his moral growth, and offloading decision-making to AI compromises his ability to act ethically. His request, supported by the American Humanist Association, emphasized that automated processing conflicts with his obligation to uphold human dignity. The university confirmed the exemption allows him to perform his role without AI requirements, though he may attend meetings with colleagues using the technology. This case highlights secular humanism's recognition as a religion, granting protections akin to other faiths. Durman is the first humanist to receive such an accommodation, following a similar case involving Unitarian Universalist Erin Maus. TechCrunch notes the case reflects broader concerns about AI's impact on critical thinking and creativity, with the American Humanist Association linking these concerns to multiple faiths. University officials stated accommodations are evaluated on a case-by-case basis as technology evolves.

item.title: El Niño floods California coasts before year’s highest tides
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: El Niño Is Already Flooding California’s Coasts—and the Year’s Highest Tides Haven’t Arrived
El Niño is causing severe coastal flooding in California before the year’s highest tides arrive. High tide floodwaters turned dry asphalt into two-foot-deep pools along Marin County’s Shoreline Highway, with the National Weather Service warning of persistent flooding through Halloween. Record-breaking October high tides in the Bay Area exceeded previous records, trapping motorists and raising concerns about electric vehicle (EV) battery risks. UC Davis ecologist Fraser Shilling warned of potential $1.5 million-per-day economic damages and catastrophic flooding in coastal towns this winter, citing government inaction. Researcher Sean Vitousek noted that spring tides alone caused one-foot-above-normal flooding, but upcoming king tides and storms could lead to worse impacts. EVs, particularly, face risks as saltwater can trigger thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries, according to fire consultant Patrick Durham. Shilling identified six regions, including San Francisco International Airport and San Luis Obispo County, as flood-prone areas. Officials in Newport Beach are distributing sandbags ahead of winter surges.

item.title: Windows 11 PC Can Reinstall Without USB Drive
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Your broken Windows 11 PC no longer needs a USB drive to come back to life
Microsoft introduces Cloud Rebuild for Windows 11, allowing users to reinstall the operating system without a USB drive. The feature enables a full reinstall even if the current system is unbootable, downloading both Windows and device drivers from Windows Update. Unlike Cloud Download, Cloud Rebuild works when the system is too damaged to boot. Users can choose to sanitize their drive, which irreversibly erases data. IT administrators can initiate the process remotely. To use Cloud Rebuild, users must connect to Wi-Fi or Ethernet, confirm the Windows build and language, and accept data loss warnings. The feature is available via the KB5127936 update for Windows 11. Users are advised to back up important files before proceeding, as the process requires a stable power source and results in data loss.

item.title: Google's AI search underperforms but plans to boost ad revenue
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
Alphabet reported Q3 2026 revenue of $128 billion, up 25% year-over-year, but stock dropped 12% post-earnings. Net income fell $9 billion compared to last year. Search growth slowed to 12% in Q3, down from 17% in Q2 and 19% in Q1. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler noted AI search queries generate less revenue than organic searches due to fewer ads and lower ad costs. Cloud revenue exceeded $30 billion, beating analyst estimates. Despite strong overall profits, Google plans to increase AI spending next year while addressing revenue gaps from AI search. Analysts expected higher earnings per share, but Google reported $2.12 versus a projected $3.02. Search volume growth remains a concern as users shift to AI chatbots for answers.

item.title: Datavault AI’s Stock Plummets After Bitcoin Access Stalls
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: AI Company’s Stock Craters After Admitting Its Bitcoin Is Stuck on an Exchange Nobody’s Heard of
Datavault AI’s stock plummeted after the company admitted it cannot access approximately $65 million in Bitcoin held on Biconomy Pte. Ltd., an obscure exchange. The Bitcoin was part of a 2025 transaction where Scilex Holding Company paid for shares and warrants with 1,328.43 Bitcoin, but Datavault sold most of it back to Scilex, leaving 817.6 Bitcoin unwithdrawable. A June 2026 term sheet proposed Scilex buying the remaining Bitcoin for $50 million, but no definitive agreement was finalized. Datavault’s SEC filing disclosed the stalled withdrawal, forcing it to reclassify the Bitcoin as a receivable and revise financial statements. Marc Hochstein noted the companies were unknown to him, referencing the crypto adage ‘not your keys, not your coins.’ Biconomy, not registered with Malaysia’s regulator, remains unresponsive to inquiries. The incident highlights risks for bitcoin treasury companies, as several have abandoned the model amid market volatility.

item.title: Reddit Shifts to Logged-In-Only Experience to Combat Traffic Decline
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Engadget, TechCrunch, PCMag Original headline: Reddit Announces Shift to Logged-In-Only Experience Amid Declining Search Traffic
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman announced a shift to a primarily logged-in user experience, citing declining search traffic and data protection needs. The change, starting with Q4 tests in non-U.S. markets, aims to improve ad targeting, user engagement, and compliance with global data regulations. Search referral traffic dropped by over 1 million weekly referrals in October, with projections of low-double-digit DAU declines if trends continue. AI-driven search tools like Google’s AI overviews have reduced traffic, which Reddit has long relied on. U.S. DAUs fell 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, while global DAUs remained flat at 130.3 million. Revenue grew 53% to $895 million, driven by ads and AI data licensing. Huffman emphasized logged-in users provide better engagement signals for personalized content and ads, and the policy addresses data scraping concerns, as unauthorized access often occurs through logged-out experiences. The platform will continue licensing data to third parties but tighten access controls. The move mirrors strategies by Facebook and LinkedIn, though challenges remain in balancing user experience with business goals. Huffman acknowledged the shift could signal a broader move away from open web access, calling it 'a big change for me' as a longtime advocate for internet accessibility. The front page will remain accessible without login, with tests on logged-in vs. logged-out boundaries.

item.title: Meta tests 'Threads Friends' for private post sharing
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Meta is testing 'Threads Friends' for sharing posts with smaller groups
Meta is testing 'Threads Friends' in Ireland, Italy, and Japan, allowing users to share posts with up to 50 followers in private groups. The feature mirrors Twitter's discontinued 'Circles' from 2022, which limited posts to 150 users. Threads automatically suggests frequent followers for the 'Friends' list, which users can customize. A preview showed a friends-only post interface and an Easter egg renaming 'Threads Friends' to 'Thriends.' The company hasn't announced expansion beyond the test regions, so U.S. users currently lack access. Users in test countries can view friends-only posts if added to the list.

item.title: VRChat Won't Add AI Labels Despite User Demand
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: VRChat says it's not adding AI labels despite user survey showing people want that
VRChat has decided not to implement AI content labels despite a user survey showing 95% of respondents want such designations. The platform's support post explains it will not add tags for AI-generated content or filter it from search results. Instead, it will consider labels for 'Human-authored' content and a 'Tools used' field, but no final decision has been made. Creators warn that some users might mislabel AI-assisted work as fully human-authored, while others could engage in 'sleuthing' behavior to identify AI content or harass creators. The post emphasizes balancing community preferences, prioritizing changes like improved thumbnails, discovery tools, and quality metrics. VRChat, used for filmmaking and safe communities for transgender users, has also faced accusations of hosting toxic behavior.

item.title: North Korean Hackers Use AI and Post-Quantum Crypto in New Attacks
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Security experts warn North Korean hackers aren't just using AI in their new campaigns, but also 'post-quantum' encryption
Kaspersky reports North Korean hackers are using AI and post-quantum encryption in new cyberattacks. Operation FlashHole, active since July 2025, targeted South Korean software, construction, and telecom firms. The Lazarus Group's updated LPEClient tool uses ML-KEM-1024, a post-quantum key exchange, to secure malware delivery. Attackers used phishing via a fake AI-tailored resume and a GitHub site linked to a command-and-control server. The malware exploited CrossWeb EX, a security tool, to gain access. Kaspersky notes the AI-generated resume and phishing tactics, with ojun Ryu stating Lazarus is integrating AI into its hacking methods. The post-quantum encryption, part of NIST standards, aims to protect data in transit against future quantum threats. While the encryption doesn't hide malware activity, it allows attackers to store encrypted payloads for later decryption. Kaspersky advises verifying links, patching systems, and monitoring cloud services like GitHub and Dropbox. The focus on software firms suggests a hunt for exploitable code, distinguishing this espionage from profit-driven attacks. The group's use of advanced cryptography highlights a strategic shift in state-sponsored hacking.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Developer Shrinks Windows 11 to 667MB for CD
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: A developer shrank Windows 11 down to just 667MB. It fits on a CD
Developer NTDEV created Pico11, a stripped-down version of Windows 11 reduced from 35GB to 667MB before installation. The ISO, totaling 883MB after installation, retains only seven core apps like Notepad and Calculator. Pico11 removes bloatware, Microsoft Edge, AI features, and Windows Update. The project, presented as a proof of concept in a YouTube video, demonstrates how Windows 11 could be minimized. NTDEV plans to release Pico11 via Tiny11 Builder, though release timing and 1GB size constraints remain uncertain. The project highlights potential for a significantly lighter Windows 11 variant.

item.title: AWS Aims for $1T Revenue, Jassy Says Spending Will Be Key
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
Andy Jassy, Amazon’s CEO, reiterated during the company’s quarterly earnings call that AWS aims to become a trillion-dollar revenue business. He emphasized the scale of the opportunity, noting AWS’s current annualized revenue run-rate is $184 billion. To support growth, Amazon plans to spend $220 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, with significant increases expected in 2027. Jassy framed the investment as essential to capitalize on a historic surge in global cloud demand driven by AI, citing AWS’s 39% year-over-year revenue growth and forecasts of 40% growth in 2027 and 2028. He called the AI boom a ‘once-in-a-lifetime opportunity’ requiring substantial upfront spending. Despite Jassy’s confidence, investors remained skeptical, with Amazon shares dropping 6% in after-market trading. Other cloud providers, like Microsoft, are also investing heavily in AI infrastructure while reporting strong revenue growth.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: User shares 5 Gmail automations to streamline inbox management
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Gmail stopped being a nightmare after I set up these 5 simple automations
A user describes five Gmail automations to reduce inbox clutter. They use starred messages as a to-do list, creating filters to automatically star emails from specific senders or containing keywords like 'action required' or 'invitation'. A template reply is set up for common business inquiries, triggered by keywords like 'enquiry' or 'request'. Emails with 'invoice' or 'payment' are forwarded to a personal account for financial tracking. A vacation responder is enabled to notify senders of unavailability. Labels are applied to categorize emails, with some messages skipped to the inbox to keep the main view clear. The user notes trade-offs, like losing notifications for skipped emails, but finds the system effective. They also suggest disabling features like Chat and Meet tabs to reduce distractions. These changes transformed their inbox from a chore to a manageable system.

item.title: Chrome extensions hijack search engines for ad money
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Your search engine could be hijacked by a Chrome extension that barely does anything
Security firm Socket found over 300 Chrome extensions that change users' default search engines, routing searches through servers controlled by the extension developers. These extensions have accumulated 13.4 million installs since 2013. Researcher John Tuckner explains they exploit Chrome's built-in setting to swap search engines without requiring code or permissions. Extensions often masquerade as useful tools like PDF converters or safe-search helpers, distributed via spammy pop-up ads outside the Chrome Web Store. While the primary goal is to earn referral payments from search engines like Bing and Yahoo, Tuckner warns the same method could enable tracking or redirect searches to phishing sites. Users should review chrome://extensions for unrecognized tools and verify their default search engine settings in Chrome's settings. Tests showed identical searches through the Predator Search extension resulted in different outcomes, highlighting potential data collection risks.

item.title: Reddit User's NAS Hacked by 18-Month-Old Ransomware Flaw
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Tech whiz's internet-accessible Synology NAS gets bit by ransomware attack from 18-month-old remote code execution flaw
Reddit user NakamuraHwang's Synology DS918+ NAS was compromised by ransomware exploiting the CVE-2024-10441 remote code execution vulnerability. The attack occurred after the device's web interface was exposed to the internet and it remained unpatched for 18 months. Despite having a 3-2-1 backup setup, the user retained data by attaching disks to a Proxmox machine. The NAS's DSM operating system used mdraid, allowing forensic analysis. Synology's update process is criticized for misleading users into believing devices are up to date, despite critical patches requiring manual installation. The company lacks a direct notification system for security vulnerabilities, and updates like PHP2Shell patches must be applied separately. Experts advise using VPNs or SSH tunnels to protect devices, as Synology's consumer-focused units still face security risks despite shifting away from consumer markets.

item.title: SALES: Satechi OnTheGo keyboard praised for built-in stand and travel durability
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: This is the physical keyboard you need if you care about typing on your phone
Reviewers recommend Bluetooth keyboards with built-in stands for phone typing. Satechi OnTheGo keyboard is highlighted for its dual-purpose stand that doubles as a protective cover. The stand secures phones and tablets, preventing wobbling during use. Reviewers note travel-friendly designs that reduce keyboard damage from bag friction. The keyboard's stand also provides a stable surface for devices like the Motorola Razr Fold. A compatible mouse is also praised for portability and performance. Stand-alone phone stands are criticized for inadequate support and size limitations. The Satechi keyboard costs $80 and is endorsed by multiple reviewers for its practicality in daily use.
